title: Tokenization-aware SLI schema and weighted error-budget burn & variant-demotion policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and standardize how SLIs are computed with tokenization-aware measurements (prompt vs completion tokens), specify a weighted error-budget burn model that accounts for token counts and model cost, and enumerate automated variant demotion / circuit-breaker behavior driven by token-weighted burn rates. This ticket formalizes the schema, the runtime signals required, and the operational playbook for graceful degradation and load shedding that preserves high-value completions.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical SLI schema that separates prompt_token_latency, first_token_latency, per_completion_token_throughput, and quality_acceptance_rate is documented and reviewed
Error-budget burn calculation defined as: burn = sum_over_requests(weight(token_count) * failure_flag) with weight profiles per-model/quantization tier
Default weight profiles (low, medium, high) provided and validated against historical traffic for at least three tenant classes
Circuit-breaker thresholds mapped to token-weighted burn rates and exposed as runtime feature flags
Variant demotion policy implemented in the router: proportional traffic shift away from burning variants when 1-, 3-, and 7-day burn windows exceed thresholds
Load-shedding behaviors (truncate, shorten-max-tokens, deny-low-priority routes) implemented and gated by both token-budget and latency SLO signals
Dashboards and alert rules created in Console showing token-weighted burn, per-variant SLI, and predicted time-to-breach for error budgets
decisions: Measure tokens via standardized tokenizer used at serving-time to avoid mismatch between client and runtime token counts
Separate SLI buckets: prompt tokens (ingest/acceptance), generation tokens (per-token latency/throughput), and quality SLI (application-defined pass/fail) to allow independent guardrails
Weighting function chosen as piecewise linear: weight = base + alpha * token_count where base captures fixed cost and alpha captures variable per-token cost; profiles tuned per model family
Circuit-breaker triggers use token-weighted burn rate on 1h/24h windows with hysteresis to avoid flapping; 1h used for immediate shedding, 24h for demotion/rollbacks
tradeoffs: Pro: token-aware burn aligns cost incentives and reduces chances of noisy short requests skewing budgets
Con: adds complexity to SLI computation and requires consistent tokenization at the runtime boundary
Pro: proportional demotion preserves capacity for higher-priority tenants vs binary failover
Con: more moving parts to test; requires robust simulation and synthetic replay to validate policy outcomes
implementation_notes: Add token_count fields to request and response telemetry with tokenizer_version metadata
Extend SLI aggregation pipeline to compute weighted burn per-tenant and per-variant; include windowed aggregates (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d)
Router: implement score-based demotion where score = burn_rate_normalized * quality_penalty; demote variants with highest score

Circuit-breaker: implement two-tier actions: (1) immediate shedding - reduce max_tokens and enable truncation for low-priority routes; (2) demotion - move traffic to cheaper variant or earlier model snapshot
Provide migration shim for existing endpoints to backfill token counts for last 90 days where possible
Ensure KMS access patterns unaffected; token telemetry must not include raw prompt content (PII rule)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (testing): simulation using last 30 days of traffic in staging to validate weight profiles and demotion logic
Phase 1 (opt-in): expose token-weighted SLI on a small set of internal tenant endpoints and gather telemetry for 14 days
Phase 2 (gradual default): enable token-weighted burn as a default for all non-enterprise routes with monitoring and auto-rollback gate
Phase 3 (policy enforcement): enable automated demotion policies for P2/P3 traffic; enterprise tenants remain opt-out until contractual changes
Rollback: clear conditions based on quality SLI regressions and unexpected U-curve in latency; fall back to unweighted error-budget if necessary
monitoring: Console dashboard: token-weighted burn per-tenant, per-endpoint, per-variant over 1h/24h/7d
Alert: token-weighted burn projected to exhaust error budget within 24h -> P1 paging
SLO health: prompt_token_95th, first_token_99th, per_token_throughput_percentiles, and quality_acceptance_rate trend
Synthetic probe: 3 synthetic prompts of short/medium/long token profiles per region to detect tokenization regressions
Audit logs: record demotion actions with rationale and pre/post traffic percentages
next_steps: Finish telemetry PR and coordinate rollout window with infra team (Jake Morales)
Run simulation job on last-90-days dataset and produce sensitivity report (owner: Jonah Kim)
Draft customer comms for enterprise tenants with opt-out instructions
Create Console panels and alert rules in collaboration with Observability team
